text: 🇲🇽🌎 "There's a relationship of respect. I have my reservations about it being President Trump." On Trump's public praise of her administration and US Homeland Security Secretary Mullin telling Congress that Sheinbaum's government has surpassed cooperation of any recent Mexican administration. — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo She accepts the recognition of the Mexican State but doesn't normalize the person or the project. The same week she's denouncing the US far-right campaign against Mexico, she keeps the diplomatic channel open without flattering it. A line, not a hug.

🇲🇽⚽ "Not just the matches — and then it leaves. Use the World Cup to build the country." Sheinbaum's frame for the Mundial Social: 1,200 new federal football fields, 1.13 million kids in the school tournament across 28,621 schools, 43% girls' participation, programs for seniors and people with Down syndrome. — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo 7 days from kickoff. The bet is that the kids playing on those new pitches become the pipeline for the next generation of professionals. World Cup as social infrastructure, not as a neoliberal storefront.

🇲🇽⚽ Iran's national team arrives in Tijuana tomorrow — because the US wouldn't let them stay. "Iran's national team arrives tomorrow in Tijuana, because they are going to train there due to some situations they have with the United States." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo Iran plays its three group-stage matches in the US — against New Zealand, Belgium and Egypt — but Washington refused to let the delegation sleep on US soil. Asked if Mexico could host them, the answer was: yes, no problem. Their base will be the Xolos training center on the Tijuana border.

🇲🇽✊ Mexico signs national tomato agreement to cut out intermediaries. "What we are seeking is to reduce those intermediaries. To have a direct agreement between the producer and whoever sells the tomato — central market, supermarket, tianguis, or any other form of commercialization." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo Producers from 18 states, central wholesale markets, tianguis and supermarket chains signed on. Targets the price spike that pushed tomato to 80 pesos/kilo this season — driven by a plague in Sinaloa and Florida plus middlemen. National market gets priority over export.

🚨🇲🇽 Sheinbaum names the calendar behind the US campaign against Mexico. "A very strong campaign has been unleashed — because of their November 2026 elections they want to use Mexico in their rhetoric, and to ally with the Mexican far-right for the 2027 election." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo Two electoral cycles, one operation: US midterms in November 2026, Mexican midterms in 2027. Mexico used as a foreign-policy prop for US domestic politics, and as fuel for the local opposition heading into the next vote. The president is naming the timeline out loud.

🔥🇲🇽 "All these neoliberal far-rightists do not believe in the concept of sovereignty." Sheinbaum tied the Mexican right's recent street provocations to the international far-right and said the throughline is the same: a refusal to accept that Mexico is a sovereign nation. — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo She read out the text of a constitutional reform her government is pushing: Mexico will not accept foreign interference in its electoral processes or investigations carried out without express authorization of the Mexican State. One of the strongest formal defenses of non-intervention of the sexenio.

🇲🇽✊ "We are living in times of definition." Sheinbaum responded to AMLO's open letter backing her government unconditionally and calling out the US offensive against Mexico as political and electoral, not a real fight against drug addiction. — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo, on AMLO's letter AMLO's letter, titled "My unconditional support for President Sheinbaum and a respectful reflection on President Trump," framed Washington's pressure on Mexico as 19th-century-style interventionism dressed up as security cooperation. Sheinbaum thanked him and said this debate is necessary.

🇲🇽🛢️ PEMEX STABILIZES — 5 STRAIGHT QUARTERS OF PRODUCTION, REFINING UP 21.9%, BIGGEST QUARTERLY VOLUME IN 11 YEARS

New Pemex director Juan Carlos Carpio Fragoso opened the 2026 Mexican Petroleum Congress in Veracruz with hard numbers: five consecutive quarters of stable crude output thanks to strategic fields, and the National Refining System now logging 1.11 million barrels/day of petroleum products — a 21.9% jump and the largest quarterly volume in 11 years. Medium-term target: 1.8 million barrels/day, after 2025 ended at the lowest daily figure since 1990. "Engineering, innovation, and technical knowledge" to consolidate Mexico's energy sovereignty, in his words. The privatization vultures said state-owned oil couldn't recover. The numbers say otherwise.
